newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA MAY SELL COFFEE TO RUSSIA - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA MAY SELL COFFEE TO RUSSIA - REPORT.

text.p: Indonesia may sell coffee to Russia under a counter-trade deal involving the purchase of Sukhoi Su-30 fighter jets and MI-17 helicopters, the Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper reported on Thursday.

The daily quoted Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters (AICE) as saying the group as been invited by the industry and trade ministry to take part in the countertrade deal.
A ministry official contacted by Reuters said he could not confirm the news, while an official of the AICE referred questions to Soedargo, who was not available for confirmation.
"The ministry of industry and trade has invited us to take part in the countertrade deal," Soedargo was quoted as telling Neraca. "We welcome the invitation."
Soedargo said he did not know how much coffee would be exported to Russia, but added the government would negotiate the sale on behalf of exporters.
Indonesia announced on Tuesday it would buy 12 Russian Sukhoi Su-30K fighter aircraft and eight Russian MI-17-1V helicopters as part of a defence modernisation plan.
The announcement followed a decision in June to cancel a deal to buy nine U.S. F-16 jets following criticism in the U.S. Congress of Indonesia's human rights record.
